question: What is the main job of the puborectalis muscle?

options.A: Regulates the flow of urine from the bladder
options.B: Pulls the pubic bone upward during heavy lifting
options.C: Rotates the thigh outward at the hip joint
options.D: Forms a sling to help maintain fecal continence

explanation: Well done! The puborectalis loops behind the rectum to create a sharp angle, helping you hold stool until you're ready to go.

question: Why is it important for the family to have a direct contact number for the psychiatric ward during a patient's leave?

options.A: So they can order extra hospital meals to be delivered
options.B: So they can negotiate a discount on hospital bills
options.C: So they can seek immediate guidance before minor challenges escalate into major crises
options.D: So they can report local weather conditions to the doctor

explanation: Having a direct phone line gives families peace of mind and lets them get professional advice before small issues become big problems.

question: Why should a patient empty their bladder right before a pelvic examination?

options.A: To measure baseline kidney function accurately
options.B: To collect a routine 24-hour urine sample
options.C: To reduce pelvic discomfort and improve organ palpation
options.D: To prevent sudden drops in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Great job! An empty bladder sits lower down, making the exam much more comfortable for the patient and allowing you to feel the reproductive organs clearly.

question: An 80-year-old patient with mild nerve numbness in their hands (neuropathy) is going home. Which safety change is most important?

options.A: Placing heavy glass mugs on the lowest possible counter shelf
options.B: Removing all rugs to prevent tripping and broken bones
options.C: Installing an automatic shut-off timer on the kitchen stove
options.D: Buying a brighter desk lamp for reading in the evening

explanation: You got it! Since neuropathy reduces feeling in the hands, an automatic stove timer prevents them from accidentally leaving burners on or misjudging hot pots.

question: A patient drops out halfway through a six-month nursing study on chronic pain. What is this called in research terms?

options.A: Testing
options.B: Attrition
options.C: Maturation
options.D: History

explanation: Attrition happens when participants leave or drop out before a study ends. It can mess up our data, so researchers always watch out for it!

question: How does unit dispensing improve financial transparency for patients?

options.A: Medication prices are standardized across all states
options.B: Hospital care becomes completely free of charge
options.C: Invoices are calculated based on hospital stay duration
options.D: Patients pay only for the exact doses administered

explanation: Instead of buying an entire pack of fifty tablets when only five are needed, the patient only pays for those five doses. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a major social challenge faced by half-way houses in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive public demand for luxury hotel-style rooms
options.B: Stigma leading to community resistance against facility locations
options.C: Too many trained psychiatrists wanting to work in the homes
options.D: An overabundance of government funding and free resources

explanation: True. Deep-seated cultural stigma often makes neighbors uneasy or resistant when a mental health facility tries to open in their neighborhood.

question: Where do microfilariae mainly travel and live in the human body?

options.A: Inside liver tissue permanently
options.B: Major arteries only
options.C: Skin and subcutaneous tissues
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Unlike some parasites that hang out strictly in the blood, these little ones love to migrate through your skin and tissues, setting off local immune reactions.

question: Which lifestyle habits are most strongly linked to squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck?

options.A: High dietary sodium and low fluid intake
options.B: Tobacco use and excessive alcohol consumption
options.C: Chronic lack of sleep and high daily stress
options.D: Excessive exposure to sunlight and wind

explanation: Tobacco and alcohol act like a double whammy, irritating and damaging the delicate lining cells of the airway over time and dramatically raising the risk of cancer. Knowledge is power!

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical challenge faced in Nigerian healthcare budgeting?

options.A: Inflation driving up the cost of imported medical drugs
options.B: Delays in the official release of approved budget allocations
options.C: Instantaneous release of excess government funds every single week
options.D: Unpredictable revenue caused by low health insurance coverage

explanation: Delayed funding releases are a known challenge, so instantaneous weekly funding is incorrect. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why is connecting a patient to community resources like vocational training important?

options.A: It forces them to work without getting any rest
options.B: It ensures the clinic makes a financial profit
options.C: It replaces the need for talking to a nurse or doctor
options.D: It helps them regain independence and purpose through meaningful activity

explanation: Community resources like job training help patients reintegrate into society and build a fulfilling life after illness. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which area of health education focuses on workplace safety and protective gear for workers?

options.A: Maternal and child health
options.B: School health
options.C: Geriatric health
options.D: Occupational health

explanation: Occupational health targets workers in factories, offices, or farms to prevent job-related injuries and illnesses.

question: How does community MHPSS nursing differ from traditional hospital-based psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It forbids the nurse from ever talking to the patient's family members
options.B: It replaces the need for medical doctors in emergency situations
options.C: It extends beyond hospital walls to train primary workers and promote mental health
options.D: It focuses solely on locking ward doors and managing physical restraints

explanation: Community nursing means stepping out of the ward! You get to educate, mentor local health workers, and promote wellness right where people live.

question: How do community nurses best advocate for marginalized or vulnerable populations?

options.A: By reporting undocumented migrants to law enforcement agencies
options.B: By advising them to relocate to wealthier neighborhoods
options.C: By setting up mobile clinics and offering free health screenings
options.D: By closing down rural health posts to save money

explanation: Brilliant! Bringing care directly to the people through outreach and free screenings is what nursing heart is all about.

question: Which of these is NOT considered a modern digital health trend in nursing?

options.A: Manual paper charting systems
options.B: Artificial intelligence tools
options.C: Wearable health monitors
options.D: Telehealth platforms

explanation: Correct! Manual paper charting is a traditional old-school method, unlike exciting digital trends like telehealth and wearables.

question: Which of these is a classic example of environmental asphyxia?

options.A: Severe diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: An acute myocardial infarction
options.C: Drowning in a swimming pool
options.D: A sudden allergic asthma attack

explanation: Environmental asphyxia happens when outside factors—like water, smoke, or a tight space—keep a person from reaching clean air. Water in a pool is a clear external block!

question: What is the first phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Diagnosis
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Planning
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: Assessment is always the starting point, where the nurse collects all necessary information about the patient. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why must drugs chosen for the formulary stay stable in tropical climates?

options.A: To make the drug containers look attractive on hospital shelves
options.B: To ensure the tablets dissolve instantly when dropped in cold water
options.C: To prevent the medicine from degrading rapidly under local weather conditions
options.D: to guarantee the medication smells pleasant during administration

explanation: Nigeria's warm weather can break down chemicals quickly. Drugs must be tough enough to hold their strength in our local climate!

question: What is the primary purpose of developmental screening tools used by nurses?

options.A: To replace formal psychological testing in schools
options.B: To flag children who need a comprehensive evaluation
options.C: To provide an immediate and final medical diagnosis
options.D: To measure the exact intelligence quotient score

explanation: Screening tools are meant to identify warning signs early so specialists can perform formal, in-depth assessments. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h5)

question: When are intravenous (IV) vasodilators and inotropes typically used for heart failure?

options.A: As a daily morning pill for patients with mild fatigue
options.B: During acute, severe decompensated episodes in the hospital
options.C: As a replacement for all dietary salt restrictions
options.D: To prevent heart failure in young, healthy athletes

explanation: You got it! IV medications are heavy-duty tools saved strictly for emergency hospital settings when a patient is in severe distress and needs rapid help.

question: What do we call the starting money or initial drug stock used to launch a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: The initial money or drug stock used to start the fund
options.B: The monthly profit withdrawn by the hospital accountant
options.C: The fine paid by patients who lose their drug prescriptions
options.D: The emergency tax collected from private pharmacies

explanation: Exactly! 'Seed capital' is just the starting push—the initial cash or drugs needed to get the revolving cycle rolling before patient payments start coming in.

question: What is the safest way for a nurse to check the strength and timing of a mum's contractions?

options.A: Ask the patient to guess how long her abdominal pain lasts
options.B: Measure the mother's blood pressure before and after every contraction
options.C: Perform frequent digital vaginal examinations every fifteen minutes
options.D: Palpate the fundus of the uterus with the fingertips over a set period

explanation: Gentle touch on the top of the uterus (the fundus) tells you everything you need to know about contractions without risking infection from too many internal exams.

question: As a nurse explaining a treatment plan, what should you avoid doing?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient does not understand
options.B: Ensuring the conversation remains strictly confidential
options.C: Explaining the importance of abstaining from sex during treatment
options.D: Asking the patient about her current sexual partners

explanation: Always keep it simple! Heavy medical grammar just confuses patients. Talk to them in clear, everyday language they can easily grasp.

question: Why should patients with a pacemaker avoid contact sports?

options.A: High impact activities cause the heart rate to become permanently fixed
options.B: Rapid arm movements will completely drain the battery within a few hours
options.C: Physical blows to the chest can damage the generator or dislodge the wires
options.D: Sweating during heavy exercise will rust the titanium case of the battery

explanation: Hard blows to the chest can break the wires or shift the device out of place. Protecting that pocket is key!

question: Why do most primary brain tumors start in neuroglial cells rather than mature neurons?

options.A: Neurons lack a cell membrane to protect against damage
options.B: Glial cells do not require oxygen or glucose supply
options.C: Neurons are too small to undergo cancerous mutations
options.D: Glial cells retain the ability to divide throughout life

explanation: Mature neurons stop dividing once we grow up, but glial cells can keep dividing. Because they keep multiplying, they are much more prone to forming tumors if things go wrong.

question: Broca's area in the brain is mainly responsible for which function?

options.A: Comprehension of written text
options.B: Recognition of familiar faces
options.C: Physical production of speech
options.D: Balance and postural stability

explanation: Fantastic! Broca's area coordinates your lips, tongue, and vocal cords so you can speak out loud clearly.

question: What is the main purpose of laws like Good Samaritan laws for healthcare workers helping in a disaster?

options.A: To guarantee that every patient receives financial compensation for injuries
options.B: To give nurses the legal right to refuse treating anyone during a crisis
options.C: To protect professionals acting in good faith from liability when providing emergency care
options.D: To remove all hospital accountability for medical malpractice occurring indoors

explanation: You got it! These laws give healthcare workers peace of mind to step up and help in emergencies without fear of being sued, as long as they act reasonably.

question: How is desiccated thyroid extract different from synthetic levothyroxine?

options.A: Both thyroxine and triiodothyronine from animal sources
options.B: Non-hormonal plant extracts that stimulate the pituitary
options.C: Only pure synthetic triiodothyronine
options.D: Chemically altered molecules designed to bypass the liver

explanation: Desiccated thyroid comes from dried animal glands, meaning it naturally carries a mix of thyroid hormones rather than just one lab-created formula.

question: How do open town hall meetings help clinical teams during a major change?

options.A: They allow hospital executives to lecture staff without interruption.
options.B: They give nurses a voice, which reduces anxiety and builds ownership.
options.C: They delay the implementation process until all staff quit.
options.D: They replace the need for hands-on clinical training entirely.

explanation: When staff have a platform to share worries, they feel valued and become active partners rather than reluctant followers.

question: Why does involving the patient in creating their medication plan improve adherence?

options.A: It ensures the hospital pharmacy never runs out of stock
options.B: It gives them a sense of ownership over their health choices
options.C: It stops all possible drug side effects from happening
options.D: It removes the need for nurses to check vital signs

explanation: When people help design a plan that fits their life, they are much more motivated to stick with it. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which level of healthcare prevention includes traditional rehabilitation activities?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Tertiary prevention is all about managing existing long-term issues, preventing complications, and getting the patient to their highest possible function.

question: Why are bedside nurses usually the best people to spot where clinical changes are needed?

options.A: They spend most of their shift working in the hospital administrative offices
options.B: They dictate national health policies and regulatory frameworks
options.C: They have final authority over hospital budget allocations
options.D: They experience daily workflows and spot operational bottlenecks firsthand

explanation: You are right at the bedside every day, so you see firsthand what slows things down or causes delays for patients. Who knows the ward better than you?

question: Which medication is routinely given during antenatal visits to protect pregnant women and babies from malaria?

options.A: Chloroquine phosphate
options.B: Amodiaquine tablets
options.C: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
options.D: Quinine hydrochloride

explanation: Well done! Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) is given at set clinic visits to clear malaria parasites from the placenta and keep the baby safe.

question: Why must honey be strictly avoided for infants under one year of age?

options.A: It contains high levels of artificial food coloring
options.B: It always causes immediate childhood obesity
options.C: It carries a severe risk of causing infant botulism
options.D: It replaces the need for essential milk feeds

explanation: Honey can contain spores of the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, which immature infant digestive tracts cannot fight off safely. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty in teenage boys?

options.A: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.B: A sudden surge in testosterone and related hormones
options.C: The full closure of the growth plates in long bones
options.D: An increase in the production of red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! A sudden rise in testosterone kicks off all those classic changes we see during adolescent growth.

question: Which of these are typically provided during specialized mental health care?

options.A: Initial safety sweeps and psychological first aid
options.B: Community dialogue meetings and traditional dance therapy
options.C: Basic food distribution and emergency shelter setup
options.D: Psychopharmacology and structured psychotherapy

explanation: Specialized care means bringing in the big tools: professional therapy and medications (psychopharmacology) managed by trained pros.

question: Which of these is a vital disease-prevention shot routinely given during pregnancy clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: Insulin pump placement
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccination
options.C: Chemotherapy infusion
options.D: Joint replacement surgery

explanation: Well done! Tetanus toxoid is a routine life-saver given during pregnancy to protect both the mother and newborn baby from tetanus.

question: Why is severe anemia especially dangerous for a woman going into labor?

options.A: She has very little reserve to survive normal blood loss during delivery
options.B: She will automatically develop eclampsia within hours
options.C: Her contractions will completely stop during the first stage
options.D: Her baby will be born with severe bone deformities

explanation: You're doing great! Every delivery involves some blood loss. A mom with low blood levels (anemia) cannot afford even a small loss without sliding into shock.

question: What is the most serious and permanent complication of untreated onchocerciasis?

options.A: Blindness
options.B: Paraplegia
options.C: Deafness
options.D: Kidney failure

explanation: Long-term eye inflammation from dying microfilariae eventually scars the eye tissue, leading to irreversible river blindness if left untreated.

question: During a disease outbreak, which of these is a core duty for a community health nurse?

options.A: Writing national health policies and approving federal budgets
options.B: Isolating entire towns by deploying armed security forces
options.C: Conducting contact tracing and educating community members on prevention
options.D: Manufacturing vaccines inside local primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! Nurses are right on the frontline—tracking down contacts, teaching families how to stay safe, and helping at the grassroots level.

question: A researcher compares lung function in patients who developed chronic bronchitis against those who did not, looking back at their past smoking habits. Which design is this?

options.A: Cross-sectional design
options.B: Ex post facto design
options.C: True experimental design
options.D: Descriptive survey design

explanation: Well done! Because the health condition already happened and the researcher is digging into past history, it is an ex post facto (after the fact) study.

question: What is a practical way to evaluate if a community mental health campaign was successful?

options.A: Counting how many flyers were thrown into the dustbin
options.B: Asking international donors how they feel from abroad
options.C: Checking if clinic attendance for early mental health support increased
options.D: Closing down the local health center to test community resilience

explanation: Tracking behavioral shifts, such as increased early clinic visits, shows whether awareness campaigns successfully translated into actual health-seeking actions. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h8)

question: Why is it important for the nose to condition inspired air before it reaches the lungs?

options.A: To increase the total volume of air the lungs can hold
options.B: To protect delicate lower airway tissues from damage
options.C: To speed up the rate of gas exchange in the alveoli
options.D: To remove all carbon dioxide from the incoming atmosphere

explanation: Warming, humidifying, and filtering incoming air prevents cold, dry, and dirty air from irritating or damaging the sensitive tissues of the trachea and lungs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is improvement fatigue in a clinical setting?

options.A: Exhaustion caused by lifting heavy patients without mechanical assistance
options.B: Feeling overwhelmed by an endless stream of new mandates and quality targets
options.C: Physical tiredness caused by walking too many miles during a night shift
options.D: A rare muscle disease that affects nurses working in intensive care

explanation: Too many overlapping projects exhaust staff mental energy, causing them to resist any further operational changes. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h6)

question: How can frontline nurses directly help prevent medicine wastage in health clinics?

options.A: By refusing to treat patients who cannot pay cash upfront
options.B: By maintaining accurate inventory records and monitoring expiration dates
options.C: By hiding extra drug supplies in private lockers for emergencies
options.D: By ordering random medications without checking clinic records

explanation: You got it! Keeping a close eye on stock and expiry dates ensures medicines are used properly before they spoil.

question: Why is interpersonal communication considered the gold standard for changing health behaviour?

options.A: It reaches thousands of people simultaneously across multiple states
options.B: It allows for direct feedback, personal questions, and tailored guidance
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for community health workers
options.D: It costs significantly less money than printing mass media flyers

explanation: Correct! Nothing beats a real conversation. One-on-one time gives patients the chance to voice their fears and get advice built just for them.

question: What is a main reason why women struggle to pass urine during or right after childbirth?

options.A: High concentration of glucose in the urine
options.B: Pressure of the foetal head on the bladder neck
options.C: Sudden complete shutdown of the glomeruli
options.D: Severe dehydration caused by hyperemesis

explanation: As the baby moves down the birth canal, the head can temporarily press on and block the urethra, making it hard to empty the bladder. Totally normal to encounter in labor wards!

question: Imagine helping out in a 6-hour bone surgery (orthopedic procedure) with continuous X-rays and heavy lifting. What is this nurse most likely to feel after?

options.A: A cough from breathing in room dust
options.B: Deep sadness from losing a patient
options.C: Back/joint pain and radiation exposure
options.D: Chemical poisoning from floor soap

explanation: Standing for long hours, lifting heavy things, and staying close to imaging equipment takes a real toll on your muscles and bones, plus radiation safety is key!

question: What happens to bile between meals when your body doesn't need it right away?

options.A: It is filtered out by the kidneys and eliminated in urine
options.B: It is broken down into simple sugars by liver enzymes
options.C: It is stored and concentrated inside the gallbladder
options.D: It is sent back to the stomach to digest proteins

explanation: When you're not eating, your gallbladder acts like a storage pouch, holding onto bile and thickening it up until you eat something fatty and it's time to squeeze it out.

question: What is the primary effect of grapefruit juice on certain medications?

options.A: Binding directly to the drug to prevent any absorption
options.B: Inhibiting intestinal enzymes and increasing drug blood levels
options.C: Speeding up kidney excretion to reduce drug effectiveness
options.D: Neutralizing the chemical pH of the drug in the stomach

explanation: Grapefruit juice blocks specific enzymes in the gut, allowing much more medication to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which ethical principle guides triage nurses to treat every patient fairly, no matter their background?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Justice
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Justice means treating everyone fairly and sharing our healthcare resources impartially, without any bias or favoritism.

question: When cancer treatment cannot cure the disease, but aims to stop tumor growth and extend life, what is this main goal called?

options.A: Palliation
options.B: Cure
options.C: Prevention
options.D: Control

explanation: You've got this! When complete cure isn't possible, 'control' is the goal—stopping the cancer from spreading further to help the patient live a longer, fuller life.

question: What happens at the end of a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) arrangement?

options.A: The private company permanently owns the hospital building
options.B: The management contract is automatically renewed forever
options.C: The facility is demolished to build commercial real estate
options.D: Ownership of the facility is transferred back to the government

explanation: As the name says, 'BOT' means the private partner builds and runs it for a set time, then hands the keys back to the government!

question: What is a common long-term result of poor eating habits within a family?

options.A: Guaranteed immunity against all infectious diseases.
options.B: Chronic malnutrition and developmental stunting in children.
options.C: Immediate improvement in community economic status.
options.D: Increased agricultural crop yields for the next season.

explanation: You got it! Consistently missing out on key nutrients prevents growing children from reaching their full physical and mental potential.

question: What usually takes up the biggest chunk of a hospital's daily budget?

options.A: Kitchen provisions
options.B: Building maintenance
options.C: Nursing labor
options.D: Office supplies

explanation: Nurses form the largest workforce in almost every hospital, which means paying nursing staff makes up the largest slice of the operational budget.

question: Which of these is officially recognized as an offense under the VAPP Act?

options.A: Job resignation without notice
options.B: Late payment of taxes
options.C: Economic abuse
options.D: Refusing to vote

explanation: That's right! The VAPP Act recognizes that denying financial support to dependents or sabotaging someone's source of income (economic abuse) is a crime.

question: What is the most common reason drug toxicity happens in a patient?

options.A: Drinking plenty of water throughout the day
options.B: Excessively high blood levels of the medication
options.C: Taking the medication exactly as prescribed
options.D: Eating fresh fruits right after taking a pill

explanation: Toxicity simply means too much of a good thing! It happens when the drug concentration in the bloodstream climbs past the safe zone.

question: Why is the traditional mechanical approach to giving medications no longer enough?

options.A: It requires doctors to write more prescriptions
options.B: It prevents nurses from charting on computers
options.C: It ignores the patient's personal routine and individual needs
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy hospital shift

explanation: Simply handing over pills without considering the person's life often leads to poor adherence and missed doses. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which common virus is most strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Herpes simplex virus
options.C: Human papillomavirus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) are the leading cause of changes in the cervix that can lead to cancer over time. Thankfully, we have vaccines now!

question: What is the primary reason lab techs treat every incoming patient sample as a biohazard?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory equipment stays warm during the night shift
options.B: To speed up the time it takes for bacteria to grow on agar plates
options.C: To prevent accidental infection of staff and the surrounding community
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing sterile glass slides

explanation: Safety first! Treating every sample like it's infectious ensures we always use proper barrier precautions to keep everyone safe.

question: Why does the healthcare team do a home assessment before a patient is discharged?

options.A: It helps identify physical barriers like stairs or narrow doors that could cause falls or limit mobility
options.B: It replaces the need for physical therapy sessions in the clinic
options.C: It proves to the doctor that the client no longer needs any assistance
options.D: It allows the hospital to bill the client for interior decorating services

explanation: Checking the home early helps spot hazards like steps or narrow doors so ramps or rails can be fitted before the patient arrives. Safety first!

question: What should you check first if the oxygen level inside the tent suddenly goes down?

options.A: The hospital's central pharmacy inventory
options.B: The expiration date of the plastic canopy
options.C: Tubing connections and canopy edge seals
options.D: The patient's blood pressure and heart rate

explanation: Always check your basics first! Loose tubing or edges that popped out from under the mattress are usually why oxygen is leaking out.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do after discovering a clinical incident?

options.A: Ensure the immediate safety and stability of the patient
options.B: Call the hospital lawyer to discuss legal liabilities
options.C: Post a warning on the hospital electronic notice board
options.D: Sit down immediately to fill out the paper incident form

explanation: Patient first, always! Clinical stabilization comes before any paperwork is touched.

question: How does passive surveillance generally collect its data?

options.A: Patients fill out online surveys from home
options.B: Clinics and labs send reports without being prompted
options.C: Health workers actively search hospital wards for cases
options.D: Government officials test every citizen yearly

explanation: Passive surveillance waits for routine reports to come in from healthcare providers. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a needle stuck in a multidose vaccine vial?

options.A: It changes the recommended dosage for pediatric clients
options.B: It provides an easy entry route for environmental bacteria
options.C: It causes the liquid vaccine to freeze too quickly
options.D: It increases the expiration date printed on the label

explanation: Leaving a needle in the stopper breaks the closed seal of the vial, allowing airborne or contact germs to contaminate the remaining doses inside. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Why is it so important to involve bedside nurses when brainstorming new change ideas?

options.A: Ward managers are legally forbidden from creating improvement plans alone
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not get involved in nursing unit management
options.C: Frontline staff are the only ones who know how to use hospital computers
options.D: Frontline nurses understand the practical reality of daily ward workflows

explanation: Exactly! Bedside nurses know what really happens on the floor, which keeps our plans realistic instead of just looking good on paper.

question: Which behavior from a nurse will immediately make a teenager shut down and stop talking?

options.A: Listening actively to the patient's concerns
options.B: Maintaining a calm and welcoming facial expression
options.C: Asking simple open-ended questions
options.D: Displaying a judgmental or scolding attitude

explanation: Spot on! Scolding or moralizing makes teens feel ashamed, leading them to hide important health information and avoid future visits.

question: What does evidence-based nursing practice combine with research evidence?

options.A: Traditional hospital routines from the past
options.B: Financial costs of medical equipment
options.C: Personal opinions of the hospital director
options.D: Clinical expertise and patient values

explanation: True evidence-based practice brings together research findings, the nurse's clinical judgment, and the preferences of the patient. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which psychological condition is commonly reported among survivors of FGM?

options.A: Antisocial personality disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Schizophrenia with auditory hallucinations
options.D: Bipolar manic depression exclusively

explanation: You're right! The trauma of the procedure, especially when done to young girls without a choice, often leads to anxiety, depression, and PTSD symptoms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why should a nurse manager look for the root cause before penalizing an error?

options.A: Many errors are caused by broken workflows rather than careless staff
options.B: Punishing staff members is illegal in all healthcare facilities
options.C: Hospital labor unions forbid managers from talking to individual nurses
options.D: Root cause analysis is only required for surgical complications

explanation: If a faulty system or bad equipment caused the mistake, punishing the nurse won't stop it from happening again to someone else.

question: Which of these is a common health problem that shows up after a major disaster?

options.A: Psychological trauma and PTSD
options.B: Increased availability of specialized surgeons
options.C: Immediate financial surplus
options.D: Enhanced community infrastructure

explanation: Great job! Survivors often deal with deep emotional distress and mental health challenges long after their physical wounds heal.

question: What do we call the trust, mutual support, and strong sense of belonging found within a tight-knit community?

options.A: Environmental hazard
options.B: Economic status
options.C: Political mandate
options.D: Social capital

explanation: Spot on! "Social capital" is just a nursing term for the strong bonds of trust and friendship that hold a neighborhood together.

question: What do we mean by the term 'opportunity cost' in health economics?

options.A: The profit a pharmaceutical company makes on a new vaccine
options.B: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
options.C: The total amount of money a hospital spends on patient medications
options.D: The discount given to patients who pay for medical care in cash

explanation: Think of opportunity cost as what you sacrifice. When you choose to spend your last Naira on transport instead of snacks, the snack is your opportunity cost! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of home health care nursing?

options.A: To help patients manage health conditions in their own living space
options.B: To replace family members in making all daily household decisions
options.C: To isolate patients from infectious community environments
options.D: To provide permanent round-the-clock intensive care for all clients

explanation: Spot on! Home health nursing is all about bringing professional care right to where the patient lives, helping them recover and manage chronic conditions comfortably. You've got this!

question: What is the primary goal of home care for patients with chronic illnesses?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members completely
options.B: Promoting stability and preventing sudden hospital readmissions
options.C: Achieving total disease cure within one week
options.D: Stopping all routine medication use permanently

explanation: Because chronic conditions cannot be cured quickly, nursing care focuses on keeping the patient stable at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h2)

question: How can nurses best support families dealing with a loved one's CJD diagnosis?

options.A: By teaching them how to reverse the disease at home
options.B: By connecting them with palliative care and support
options.C: By promising a full recovery with experimental drugs
options.D: By restricting all visiting hours to prevent stress

explanation: Spot on! A CJD diagnosis is heartbreaking for families. Guiding them to palliative care and emotional support resources makes a world of difference.

question: Why is it important to be transparent and honest when a community health project falls short of its goals?

options.A: It ensures that all nurses involved get fired immediately
options.B: It is required to stop international sanctions
options.C: It prevents the community from ever asking for help again
options.D: It maintains community trust and helps everyone learn what to improve

explanation: Brilliant! Being honest about setbacks builds deep trust and gives everyone a chance to do even better next time. You're thinking like a true professional nurse!

question: A nurse is planning care for a newly admitted patient with severe depression and a history of job loss. What should the nursing care plan include?

options.A: Strict bed rest with zero communication until the patient asks for help
options.B: Telling the patient to forget about their job loss and think positively
options.C: Both biological treatments like medication and social support for coping with stress
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately before addressing any emotional issues

explanation: Because mental disorders have multiple causes, effective nursing care combines medical, psychological, and social interventions. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h8)

question: During an investigation, a manager finds that three other experienced nurses would have made the exact same mistake due to a confusing chart layout. What does this mean?

options.A: Individual accountability is the only factor to address
options.B: The nursing school that trained them needs to be investigated
options.C: The error comes from a system design flaw, not personal recklessness
options.D: All four nurses should face immediate disciplinary suspension

explanation: If your peers make the same slip under those conditions, it's a trap in the system, not bad nursing!

question: Why do standard health programs sometimes fail when trying to help marginalized groups?

options.A: They focus exclusively on wealthy urban business owners
options.B: They are always illegal under Nigerian state legislation
options.C: They often ignore specific social and economic barriers faced by those groups
options.D: They require patients to hold international passports

explanation: A one-size-fits-all approach often misses the unique financial, cultural, or physical hurdles that vulnerable people face every day.

question: What is the main purpose of 'socialization' within any community?

options.A: Building roads and bridges for commercial transport vehicles
options.B: Collecting taxes to fund government healthcare projects
options.C: Isolating sick patients from healthy members of the public
options.D: Passing down cultural beliefs, rules, and values to new members

explanation: Well done! Socialization is how we learn our society's customs, values, and traditions from generation to generation.

question: Your patient is healing from a deep surgical wound. Which nutrient should you make sure they get more of to help repair their tissues?

options.A: Fats
options.B: Carbohydrates
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Proteins are the building blocks of cells! When a patient has a wound to heal, they need extra protein to build new tissue and recover faster.

question: Why must a nurse check their license jurisdiction before giving tele-nursing care?

options.A: It guarantees the nurse will receive a higher salary from the government.
options.B: Nurses must be legally authorized to practice in the physical location where the patient is situated.
options.C: Patients prefer nurses who live in foreign countries.
options.D: It ensures the tele-health software will run without internet connection issues.

explanation: Always remember: legally, you can only practice where you hold a valid license to protect your patients and your career.

question: The night-shift and day-shift nurses constantly argue over who leaves more work behind. What conflict is this?

options.A: Intergroup conflict
options.B: Interpersonal conflict
options.C: Intragroup conflict
options.D: Intrapersonal conflict

explanation: Since the dispute is between two distinct groups of workers, it's an intergroup conflict. Excellent practice!

question: Which patient might have a high Body Mass Index (BMI) classification that does NOT accurately reflect excess body fat?

options.A: An elderly patient experiencing severe muscle wasting
options.B: A malnourished child with chronic protein deficiency
options.C: A professional weightlifter with high muscle mass
options.D: A sedentary patient with advanced kidney disease

explanation: Muscle tissue is much denser than fat, meaning very muscular people can have a high BMI despite having low body fat. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the main job of an analgesic drug?

options.A: To relieve pain without causing unconsciousness
options.B: To reduce high body temperature quickly
options.C: To put the patient into a deep sleep
options.D: To lower elevated blood pressure readings

explanation: Analgesics are medicines that chase away pain while keeping your patient awake and alert so you can still talk to them!

question: Why is 'activity pacing' so important when working with chronic patients in rehab?

options.A: Pacing ensures that nurses do not have to assist with patient transfers.
options.B: Hospital policies state that therapy cannot exceed twenty minutes per day.
options.C: Pushing patients past their physical limits can cause exhaustion and hinder overall recovery.
options.D: Chronic conditions make patients completely immune to physical fatigue.

explanation: You got it! Balancing therapy with enough rest prevents burnout and keeps the patient energized for their recovery journey.

question: In patient safety, what do we call a 'slip' during a procedure?

options.A: An intentional choice to ignore hospital policy
options.B: A failure to diagnose a patient properly on admission
options.C: An error of execution where the physical action fails
options.D: A complete lack of clinical knowledge about a disease

explanation: A slip happens when you know what to do in your head, but your hands briefly mess up the physical step—like hitting the wrong infusion button by accident. It happens to the best of us!

question: Why do nurses check drug information guides instead of relying only on memory?

options.A: Physicians expect nurses to memorize every single medication detail
options.B: Pharmacological knowledge changes constantly and new safety data emerges daily
options.C: Printed textbooks are legally required to be present at every bedside
options.D: Hospital policies forbid nurses from relying on their personal memory

explanation: You got it! New drugs and safety updates come out all the time, so checking reliable sources keeps our patients safe from outdated info.

question: Why is encapsulation often used specifically for pharmaceutical waste?

options.A: To turn expired tablets into sweet-tasting liquid syrups
options.B: To immobilize chemical drugs and prevent them from entering water supplies
options.C: To bleach colored medicine bottles so they can be recycled
options.D: To make heavy metal containers easier to burn in an incinerator

explanation: Encapsulation binds drugs in a solid matrix like cement, stopping them from dissolving and leaching into soil and groundwater. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why is it tricky to study things like pain and fatigue in patients?

options.A: They only occur in male patients
options.B: They are abstract and hard to define uniformly
options.C: They never change over the course of an illness
options.D: They cannot be recorded on any medical chart

explanation: Exactly! Pain and fatigue look and feel different to every single person, which makes them harder to measure the same way every time.
